test.title: Dressing for winter walks
textTitles: Dressing in layers for winter walks

texts.title: Dressing in layers for winter walks

paragraphs.text: For walking in cold weather, experts recommend several thin layers rather than one thick coat. Layers trap warm air between them and can be removed if you get too hot.
The layer next to the skin, called the base layer, should draw sweat away from the body. Wool and synthetic fabrics do this well, while cotton stays wet and makes you cold.
Over this goes a mid layer, such as a fleece, which provides most of the warmth. The outer layer, or shell, should be windproof and waterproof but allow moisture to escape.

Heat is quickly lost from the head and hands, so a hat and gloves are essential, and thick socks help to keep the feet warm. Walkers should also carry a spare layer in their bag in case the weather changes.
Finally, walkers should tell someone where they are going and when they expect to return, particularly in remote areas.
